purpose: Voriconazole injection is used to treat serious and potentially life-threatening fungal infections. It is commonly used for infections caused by fungi like Aspergillus and Candida. This medicine is typically given when the infection is severe enough to require treatment through an IV (intravenous) line.
how_it_works: Voriconazole works by attacking and destroying the outer layer (called the cell membrane) of the fungus. Without this protective layer, the fungus cannot survive and eventually dies. Basically, it stops the fungus from growing and spreading in your body.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include changes in vision such as blurry vision or seeing bright spots or colors, nausea, vomiting, rash, fever, headache, and elevated liver enzymes (which your doctor will monitor with blood tests). Many people also notice sensitivity to sunlight, so it is important to protect your skin when outdoors.
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver problems, so your doctor will regularly check your liver with blood tests. It can also affect your heart rhythm, so let your doctor know if you have any heart conditions. Avoid direct sunlight and tanning beds as this drug can make your skin very sensitive to UV light. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as voriconazole can interact with many drugs. It should not be used during pregnancy as it may harm the baby.
typical_dosing: The dose is carefully calculated based on your body weight and the type of infection being treated. It is given directly into a vein (IV) by a healthcare professional, usually every 12 hours. Your doctor will determine the exact dose and how long you need treatment, which can range from a few days to several weeks depending on how well you respond.
